summary.name: Archival science
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia article describing archival science, the study and theory of building, curating, preserving and describing archives of documents, recordings and other materials.
use_cases: planning preservation of physical and digital records
summary.what_it_does: This is an encyclopedia article, not a software tool. It explains archival science as the study of acquiring, appraising, storing, preserving and arranging archival collections. It covers the principle of provenance and original order, and history from diplomatics to the Dutch 1898 manual. It also describes description standards such as RAD and DACS, metadata standards such as MARC, EAD and Dublin Core, and digital preservation concerns. It ends with critical archival studies, graduate education and professional associations.
notable: Explains the principle of provenance and respect des fonds
Covers archival description standards RAD, DACS and EAD
Summarises digital preservation and metadata's role in it
Lists professional archivist associations and regional bodies
caveats: Describes a field of study rather than software; the awesome-selfhosted listing is for digital archiving tools, which this page does not name
Notes there is no universal set of laws or standards governing archival institutions
